sub_theme: The Great Fire of London: What Happened?

lessons.title: Introducing the Great Fire of London
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the basic outline of the Great Fire of London.
success_criteria: I can say when and where it happened.
I can say how it started.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of the Great Fire and predict what's happening.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read/tell the story of the Great Fire of London (1666, Pudding Lane bakery), modelling retelling.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence picture cards of the Great Fire's key events.
resources_needed: Great Fire of London picture/story resource

differentiation.greater_depth: Retell the whole story independently with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and retelling of a historical narrative — evidence for ENG.R2/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the outline of the Great Fire story.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family how the Great Fire started.

lessons.title: The Number 1666: Place Value
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explore place value in the number 1666 in a simple way.
success_criteria: I can say the number 1666.
I can identify the digits in the number.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at the number 1666 and discuss it's the year of the Great Fire.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Simply introduce that 1666 has 4 digits, discussing its size compared to numbers they know.
lessons.independent_task: Children explore and record facts about the number 1666 (how many digits, compare to their age/year).

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare 1666 to the current year and discuss the difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early exposure to larger numbers in context — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the year you were born compared to 1666.

lessons.title: Why Did the Fire Spread So Quickly?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain a reason the fire spread quickly.
success_criteria: I can name one reason the fire spread.
I can describe London's houses at the time.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the fire's start from earlier.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss reasons the fire spread quickly (wooden houses close together, narrow streets, strong wind, thatched roofs).
lessons.independent_task: Children record 2-3 reasons the fire spread, using pictures/simple sentences.
key_questions: Why did the fire spread so fast?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note historical causal reasoning skill — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap reasons for the fire's rapid spread.
lessons.home_link: Compare your house to a wooden 1666 house.

lessons.title: Writing a Diary Entry: Pudding Lane, 1666
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple diary entry in role as a Great Fire eyewitness.
success_criteria: I can write 'I' sentences about what I saw.
I can include a feeling.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a diary entry is.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a diary entry in role as someone watching the fire, including feelings.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a short diary entry in role, describing what they see and feel.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing in role and use of first person — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share diary entries with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Read your diary entry to your family.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction: Days of the Fire
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction problems linked to the fire's timeline (4 days).
success_criteria: I can solve a problem about the number of days.
I can show my working.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the fire lasted roughly 4 days.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model simple word problems using the fire's 4-day timeline (e.g. 'if it started on day 1, what day did it end?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve simple addition/subtraction problems related to the fire's timeline.
key_questions: How many days did the fire burn?

differentiation.support: Use a number line with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of addition/subtraction to a historical context — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Count 4 days forward from today and see what date that is.

lessons.title: How Did People Try to Stop the Fire?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a method used to try to stop the Great Fire.
success_criteria: I can name a way people tried to stop the fire.
I can say if it worked.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what people might have tried to do to stop a fire without modern equipment.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss methods used (bucket chains, fire hooks pulling down houses, firebreaks), and their limited success.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label a method used to try to stop the fire.
key_questions: Why didn't it work well at first?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of historical problem-solving attempts — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap methods used to fight the fire.
lessons.home_link: Compare old firefighting methods to modern fire engines.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading 1666-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words related to the Great Fire.
success_criteria: I can blend and read fire-themed words.
I can read a sentence about the Great Fire.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending Great Fire-themed words (e.g. 'flame', 'smoke', 'burn').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading Great Fire words over the week.

lessons.title: Shapes in Old London Buildings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D and 3D shapes in historical building pictures.
success_criteria: I can find a shape in a building picture.
I can name it correctly.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Look at pictures of 1666 London buildings, identifying shapes within the architecture.
lessons.independent_task: Children find and record shapes seen in historical building pictures.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied cross-curricularly — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap shapes found in old buildings.
lessons.home_link: Find shapes in buildings on your street.

lessons.title: What Happened After the Fire?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one change made after the Great Fire.
success_criteria: I can name one change made after the fire.
I can say why it was made.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what might need to happen after such a big fire.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that London was rebuilt with brick instead of wood, and wider streets, to prevent future fires.
lessons.independent_task: Children record one change made after the fire and why it helped.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of consequence and change — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap changes made after the Great Fire.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what your house is built from and why it's safer than 1666 houses.

lessons.title: Great Fire Hot-Seating
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to ask and answer questions in role as a Great Fire eyewitness.
success_criteria: I can ask a question about the fire.
I can answer in role.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts learned about the Great Fire this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating in role as a 1666 Londoner.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children take turns hot-seating as a Great Fire eyewitness.

differentiation.greater_depth: Ask and answer unprompted with historical detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and historical knowledge application — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap interesting answers given in role.
lessons.home_link: Role-play being a Great Fire eyewitness for your family.

lessons.title: Grouping and Sharing: Buckets in a Chain
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve grouping/sharing problems using a firefighting bucket-chain context.
success_criteria: I can group objects equally.
I can share objects equally.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap grouping and sharing from Week 4.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a grouping/sharing problem (e.g. 'share 12 buckets equally between 3 people').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve grouping/sharing problems in a bucket-chain context using counters.
key_questions: How many groups can you make?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record grouping/sharing fluency — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing objects equally at home.

lessons.title: Samuel Pepys: Who Was He? (Introduction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say who Samuel Pepys was and why he is important to this history.
success_criteria: I can say Samuel Pepys wrote a diary.
I can say why his diary is useful to historians.
lessons.starter_activity: Show a picture of Samuel Pepys.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce Samuel Pepys as someone who kept a diary describing the fire, useful as a historical source.
lessons.independent_task: Children record who Samuel Pepys was and why his diary matters, ready for deeper study next week.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the value of eyewitness sources

lessons.assessment_notes: Note introduction to primary source concept, to be built on next week — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Ask your family if they keep a diary and why.

lessons.title: Great Fire Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the Great Fire of London.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's Great Fire vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a short Great Fire passage, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why do you think people were scared?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing
differentiation.greater_depth: Answer inference questions with full-sentence reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Retell the Great Fire story to your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number, Shape, Grouping
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number, shape, and grouping skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can solve number problems in context.
I can find shapes in pictures.
I can group/share equally.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of number problems, shape identification, and grouping/sharing.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 9 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2/N3/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising this week's maths skills over the weekend.

lessons.title: Great Fire Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the Great Fire of London learned this week.
success_criteria: I can say when and how the fire started.
I can say one thing that changed afterwards.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about the Great Fire.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Great Fire of London' display combining diary entries, drawings, and facts from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about the Great Fire?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, ready to explore Samuel Pepys's diary in depth next week — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Great Fire of London' display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the Great Fire with your family.
